weaknesses: The assumption commentary is mostly renaming, not discussion. Each assumption is followed by a sentence of the form "\Cref{obj:ass:no-defiers} is the instrument monotonicity condition" or "\Cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling} is the independent sampling condition", which tells the reader nothing about plausibility or restrictiveness. In \cref{sec:setup} replace these with two or three sentences each that say what the condition rules out in the motivating training-program setting (e.g. for selection exclusion: an offer that changes employment other than through program receipt, such as an offer-triggered job-search requirement, violates it) and what evidence would make it credible.

The refutable content of the model is never stated. \cref{obj:prop:capacity-identification} implies that the observed instrument contrasts must be cellwise nonnegative (\(\ell_i(x)\ge0\), \(h_j(x)\ge0\)), and the estimator's projection step \(\widehat c_n=\Pi_{\mathfrak C}(\widetilde c_n)\) silently repairs violations of exactly that implication. Add a short subsection after \cref{obj:prop:capacity-identification} stating that these inequalities are testable implications of the maintained restrictions and that the projection in \cref{obj:def:plugin-endpoint-estimator} imposes rather than tests them, so a diagnostic report of raw negative capacities should accompany any application.

Weak selection monotonicity is treated as an input without discussing the cost of letting \(d(x)\) vary by cell. The paper notes only that "The direction \(d(x)\) is allowed to vary across covariate cells"; it should say that the direction is not chosen by the analyst but pinned by the sign of \(\Delta q(x)\) except on the zero-gap face, and discuss the substantive content of assuming that within a cell no complier is made unemployed by treatment while another is made employed. One added paragraph after \cref{obj:ass:weak-selection-monotonicity} would carry this.

The practical width of the guaranteed interval is never assessed, so the reader cannot judge the guard's usefulness. With \(A_{n,\alpha}=64K|\mathcal X|\varepsilon_Z^{-2}b_{n,\alpha}+|\mathcal X|\eta_n\) and \(b_{n,\alpha}=\sqrt{|\mathcal E|/(4n\alpha)}\), the radius \(g_{n,\alpha}\) scales roughly as \(K^{3/2}|\mathcal X|^{3/2}\varepsilon_Z^{-2}m_\star^{-1}(n\alpha)^{-1/2}\) and will equal its cap of 1 at any realistic sample size for even moderate \(K,|\mathcal X|\). In \cref{sec:inference}, report \(g_{n,\alpha}\) for the three-level witness at, say, \(\alpha=0.05\) and a range of \(n\), and state affirmatively that the guarantee is a finite-sample containment statement whose constants are conservative, with calibration left to the program in \cref{sec:limitations}.

The comparison with the trimming-bounds literature is asserted at the level of "selection direction" but never made concrete about targets. Lee-style and Chen--Flores-style bounds concern selected-complier outcome means or distributions, whereas \(\theta=P(Y_1>Y_0\mid S_1=S_0=1,C)\) is a same-unit ordinal comparison that no marginal-based trimming bound identifies. Add two sentences in \cref{sec:related-literature} making that distinction explicit, and say what the present capacities share with those constructions (the same cellwise submeasures) versus what is new (the exact-mass coupling over pairs).

The verification footnote and the theorem it decorates disagree about what is imported. \cref{obj:thm:no-selection-reduction}'s displayed conclusions (\(\Delta q(x)=0\), \(\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^0\), and the two normalized cut identities) are self-contained algebra proved in the appendix, yet the footnote says "This result uses the published conclusion \citep{LuDingDasgupta2018} ... If that cited conclusion is false, the portions of this result that depend on it are not certified." Either restate the theorem so the imported claim (that the normalized formulas coincide with the published sharp bounds) is part of the statement, or move the citation dependence into the surrounding prose and drop it from the footnote.
defects: Every roadmap cross-reference in the introduction is undefined: "\Cref{sec:related-literature} discusses...", "\Cref{sec:setup}", "\Cref{sec:sharp-bounds}", "\Cref{sec:algorithm-example}", "\Cref{sec:inference}", "\Cref{sec:limitations}". No `\label` is attached to any of those sections (only `sec:deferred-proofs` carries one), so all six render as broken references. Add the labels, and rename `sec:related-literature` to match the actual heading "Related work".

Symbol collision in the statement of \cref{obj:prop:capacity-identification}: "Let \(S\) be a five-node potential-outcome slate with covariate \(X\), binary \(Z,D,S\)" uses \(S\) both for the slate system and for the selection indicator in the same sentence. Rename the slate to \(\mathcal S\) or drop the naming entirely.

\cref{obj:def:observable-capacities}, which introduces the paper's central observable objects, does not define them: "let \(\ell_i(x)\) and \(h_j(x)\) be the lower-arm and upper-arm selected-complier outcome capacities obtained from the corresponding conditional instrument contrasts."
